description.short_caption: Lung tissue, HE stain, showing granulomatous inflammation at 200x magnification.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows lung tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (HE) at 200x magnification. The tissue exhibits granulomatous inflammation, characterized by clusters of inflammatory cells, including macrophages and lymphocytes. Central necrosis is visible, surrounded by cellular aggregates. The presence of multinucleated giant cells is also noted, which is typical in granulomatous diseases.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral lung fields and mediastinal structures.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph displaying the thoracic cavity. Both lung fields are visible, with clear visualization of the ribs, mediastinum, and diaphragm. No obvious consolidation, effusion, or masses are apparent. The cardiac silhouette appears normal in size and shape, and the trachea is midline. The image is de-identified and includes standard radiographic markers.

description.short_caption: Axial chest CT showing bilateral pulmonary abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral pulmonary findings. There are areas of increased attenuation in both lungs, suggestive of consolidation or infiltrates. The mediastinum appears central, and no significant pleural effusion is visible. The scan is likely performed with contrast, as vascular structures are well-defined.

description.short_caption: Lung tissue stained with GMS showing fungal elements.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a histopathological section of lung tissue stained with Gomori methenamine silver (GMS). The stain highlights oval to crescent-shaped fungal elements with thick, darkly stained walls against a green background. These structures are consistent with fungal spores or yeast forms. The GMS stain is commonly used to identify fungal organisms in tissue sections.
visible_findings: green background typical of GMS stain

description.short_caption: Lung tissue, H&E stain, showing granulomatous inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows lung tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) at 40x magnification. A central area of granulomatous inflammation is visible, characterized by a collection of epithelioid macrophages and surrounding lymphocytes. There are also multinucleated giant cells present within the granuloma. The surrounding lung parenchyma shows evidence of inflammation and possible tissue damage. Blood vessels are visible in the background, stained red.

description.short_caption: Histopathology of lung tissue showing a parasitic structure, HE stain, 400x magnification.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows lung tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (HE) at 400x magnification. A prominent oval-shaped parasitic structure with a thick, eosinophilic wall and internal granular contents is visible, likely representing an organism such as a helminth or its egg. Surrounding the structure are inflammatory cells, including eosinophils, and disrupted tissue architecture, indicative of a host immune response.
visible_findings: oval parasitic structure with thick wall
internal granular contents within the structure
